extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in psychology, social psychology, and humor studies (academics studying humor and related empirical work)
extracted.subtask_description: Theory-driven criteria and operational definitions for when a stimulus will be perceived as humorous across domains (entertainment, consumer products, social interaction). Focuses on comparing incongruity definitions and proposing the benign violation account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of humor (three indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is a psychological response characterized by the positive emotion of amusement, the appraisal that something is “funny,” and the tendency to laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor can be indicated by at least one of three responses: behavioral (laughing), cognitive (appraising something as "funny"), or emotional (experiencing amusement). Use measures tapping any of these to operationalize perceived humor. The authors refer to a stimulus as humorous to the extent that it elicits greater perceptions of humor (on average).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity conceptualized as Surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity defined as something unexpected or surprising — a divergence between an expected and an actual state of affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical formulations: 'deviation from expectations' or 'the cognitive conflict that arises when something unexpected happens.' Limitations: surprise lacks specificity (pleasant or unpleasant surprises are often not humorous) and lacks generality in some contexts (e.g., repeated exposures can remain humorous even when no longer surprising). Empirically, surprise alone did not predict perceived humor in the authors' studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity conceptualized as Juxtaposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity defined as the contrast or juxtaposition of two perceptions, concepts, or elements that do not normally go together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include simultaneous activation of incompatible scripts or combining disparate ideas/features. Juxtaposition may be necessary for humor but is not sufficient—juxtaposition often produces art, awe, or innovation (e.g., pop art, novel products) rather than humor. The benign violation account accepts juxtaposition as necessary but requires additional appraisals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity conceptualized as Atypicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity defined as something that departs from typical mental patterns or normal expectations (something atypical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atypical events can be positive (winning lottery) or negative (accident) and are not inherently violations. Many atypical occurrences elicit joy or sadness, not humor. Atypicality therefore lacks the specificity to distinguish humorous from nonhumorous stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incongruity conceptualized as Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incongruity defined as a disparity between the way things are and the way they should be — i.e., a violation (something that seems threatening, wrong, or negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations have negative valence (irrational, improper, inappropriate) and include threats to physical well-being, identity, social norms, language/grammar, or logical expectations. Violations differ conceptually from surprise/atypicality because they threaten a belief about how things should be; however, violations are often not humorous on their own and can produce anger, fear, or disgust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benign Violation Hypothesis (three conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor occurs when (a) something is appraised as a violation, (b) the same thing is appraised as benign, and (c) the two appraisals are juxtaposed (simultaneously present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrows incongruity by requiring the specific juxtaposition of violation and benign appraisal. The hypothesis incorporates violation and juxtaposition definitions of incongruity and explains why some violations are funny (harmless, distant, or reinterpretable) while others are not. Use manipulations or measures that separately assess violation appraisal and benignness (e.g., concern) and test their interaction/simultaneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary conditions that facilitate a benign appraisal
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors that make a violation more likely to be appraised as benign: resolution, psychological distance, safety, play cues, and a non-serious context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions are not alternatives to benignness but mechanisms that help stimuli be perceived as benign (e.g., resolution makes unexpectedness sensible; psychological distance makes threats feel less real; play or safety cues make physical threats seem harmless). When designing or evaluating humorous stimuli, consider whether these conditions are present to support a benign appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution (incongruity-resolution) as a facilitator
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution is the process of making sense of something that initially seems unexpected or illogical (finding an alternative explanation, conflicting norm, or solution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution often explains scripted jokes and puns (e.g., a punchline becomes sensible). Resolution can make an incongruity feel benign by providing an alternative interpretation. Measurement guidance: separately evaluate whether a surprising or abnormal event is resolved (presence of a conflicting rule/norm, alternative explanation, or solution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of violations to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations include threats to physical well-being, identity threats, social-norm violations, linguistic/communication violations, or logical/expectation violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different domains of violation may interact with benignness factors differently (e.g., harmless physical threats like tickling vs. real injury). When evaluating humor, classify what kind of norm or expectation is violated to predict emotional response and likelihood of benign appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinants of whether a violation seems benign
rubrics_metrics.description: A violation is more likely to seem benign when: (1) the situation seems playful rather than serious; (2) there is a conflicting rule or norm that makes the behavior seem acceptable; (3) there is an alternative explanation/interpretation; (4) the perceiver lacks strong commitment to the threatened norm/target; (5) there is psychological distance (time, spatial, social, or reality distance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these five dimensions explicitly to predict or manipulate benignness. Example: misspellings in a pun may seem benign because an alternative (homonym) explanation exists; jokes disparaging an out-group may seem benign to those who lack commitment to the targeted norm or are psychologically distant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a useful explanatory theory (predictive specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A causal theory of humor should be present when the phenomenon (humor) is observed and absent when it is not; it should maximize hits (explain occurrences of humor) while minimizing false positives (predicting humor where it does not occur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper critiques broad incongruity definitions because they are too general and produce false positives (e.g., joy, awe, or tragedy being mispredicted as humor). The benign violation account is offered as a narrower theory that increases specificity. When evaluating theories or constructing stimuli, prioritize specificity and the ability to rule out non-humorous positive/negative responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational measurement definitions (appendix measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational definitions used in the studies for coding/evaluation: Surprise (unexpectedness), Resolution (whether surprise/abnormality is made sense of), Abnormal (departure from typical patterns), Violation (something that challenges well-being/identity/beliefs), Benign (feels 'okay'), and Juxtaposition (two things not normally together).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendices instruct raters to evaluate each emotional part of a stimulus separately (e.g., is this segment surprising? is the violation benign?). Resolution is operationalized via presence of conflicting rule/norm, alternative explanation, or solution. Benignness is operationalized via the five determinants (situation, conflicting norm, alternative explanation, lack of commitment, distance). Use separate items to measure surprise, violation, benignness, and concern (concern indicates absence of benign appraisal).
